facts.claim: An A2A agent publishes an agent card, a JSON file at /.well-known/agent-card.json on its domain that names the agent, describes it, and lists its address, version, capabilities, input and output types and skills (A2A specification 1.0.0).

An A2A task moves through states including submitted, working, input-required, completed, failed and canceled; completed, failed, canceled and rejected end it, while input-required and auth-required pause it until the client answers (A2A specification 1.0.0).
The A2A specification’s latest release is version 1.0.0, after 0.1.0, 0.2.6 and 0.3.0.
The Linux Foundation launched the Agent2Agent project on 23 June 2025, seeded with the protocol Google created, with AWS, Cisco, Google, Microsoft, Salesforce, SAP and ServiceNow.

Google announced the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2) in September 2025 with more than 60 organisations: a person signs an intent mandate with price limits and timing up front, and a cart mandate fixes the exact items and price; both are cryptographically signed.
Google describes AP2 as usable as an extension of the A2A protocol and the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
On 28 April 2026 the FIDO Alliance said Google’s AP2 and Mastercard’s Verifiable Intent would be developed further in its Payments Technical Working Group.

AP2’s own site lists release v0.2 and the FIDO donation, and names a checkout mandate (the items and terms agreed with the merchant) and a payment mandate (the payment against one instrument), each a signed, tamper-evident credential.

Stripe and OpenAI released the Agentic Commerce Protocol on 29 September 2025; its Shared Payment Token lets an agent start a payment without seeing the card, and is scoped to one merchant and one basket total.

The Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP), co-developed by Google, Shopify, Etsy, Wayfair, Target, Walmart and others by its own site’s list, covers discovery, carts, checkout and orders, takes payments through AP2’s mandates and works with MCP and A2A.
The Model Context Protocol connects AI applications to outside tools and data over JSON-RPC; its current specification is dated 2026-07-28.
On WebArena’s realistic websites the best GPT-4-based agent finished 14.41% of tasks end to end, against 78.24% for people (Zhou et al., 2023).
Instructions hidden in data an AI application reads can steer it without the attacker ever talking to it: indirect prompt injection (Greshake et al., 2023).
Red-teaming a shopping agent built on AP2 found that simple adversarial prompts reliably subverted the agent’s behaviour (Debi, Zhu and Sen Gupta, 2026).
